stem: Sameer must tile a $8$ cm by $6$ cm rectangle with identical squares that fill it with no gaps and no overlaps.

parts.text: Which claim plans the tiling correctly?

options.text: Any square side works if the area $48$ is divisible by that side.
The square side must be a common divisor of $8$ and $6$, so sides such as $2$ cm work because both lengths split into equal segments.
Only a $8$ cm square can be used, matching the longer side alone.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice that names which segments must be equal.

part_answers.answer: Along each side the square side must repeat an integer number of times, so the side length must divide both 8 and 6; 2 cm divides both and tiles the rectangle.

teacher.key_rationale: Identical squares need equal side segments along both edges; side must divide 8 and 6. Area divisibility alone or matching only the long side fails that plan.
